title: A Wild Thanksgiving: Storms, Power Outages and a Parade Moved to Saturday
summary:
Thanksgiving week brought wild weather to much of the United States. A huge storm moved from the Midwest to New York City. By Thanksgiving evening, almost one million people had lost power.

Travel was hard, too: more than 400 flights were cancelled on Thursday and more than 2,000 were delayed, while about 81.5 million people were expected to travel, the AAA said.

Floods hit several places. Parts of Old Town Alexandria and Atlantic City were under water, with close to 2 to 3 feet of water in some low areas of Atlantic City.

Out west, big waves and high tides called King Tides hit the California coast. Part of the Pacifica Pier fell down on Wednesday. Central Park had its wettest Thanksgiving ever, with 1.82 inches of rain.

The weather even moved the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday — the first time ever — because strong winds made it unsafe to fly the giant balloons.

Meanwhile, shoppers got ready for Black Friday. The National Retail Federation expects about 183 million shoppers and more than $1 trillion in holiday sales.
why_it_matters: Wild weather can change your family's holiday plans, from travel and power at home to whether a parade you hoped to watch still happens.

background_read: Thanksgiving is a holiday in the United States when many families travel to get together for a big meal.
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is a famous parade in New York City with giant balloons, marching bands, and floats.
Black Friday is the big shopping day right after Thanksgiving, when many stores offer special deals and lots of people go out to shop.
Article_Structure: WHO: People across the United States, travelers, shoppers, and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
WHAT: A huge storm brought heavy rain, floods, power outages, and cancelled flights during Thanksgiving week, and the parade was moved to Saturday.
WHERE: Across the United States, from the Midwest to New York City, and along the California coast.
WHY: Strong winds made it unsafe to fly the parade's giant balloons, and the storm caused floods and power outages.
